title: Beyond Hate: Differentiating Uncivil and Intolerant Speech in Multimodal Content Moderation
measurement_description: The paper evaluated 'Religious Intolerance' as a specific sub-dimension of intolerant speech in multimodal memes. It measured how well vision-language models and coarse 'hatefulness' benchmark labels capture hateful, discriminatory, or prejudicial speech directed at individuals or groups based on their religion.
findings: The study found that 'Religious Intolerance' is captured reliably by the original coarse 'hatefulness' label in the Hateful Memes benchmark. Memes annotated for religious intolerance had a 91% probability of being labeled hateful in the original dataset, showing a strong positive correlation (phi = 0.37). In logistic regression analysis, the presence of religious intolerance significantly increased the odds of the content being classified as hateful.
references: Badour, J.; and Brown, J. A. 2021. Hateful Memes Classification Using Machine Learning. In 2021 IEEE Symposium Series on Computational Intelligence (SSCI), 1–8.
